definitions.type: family of Euclidean metric spaces indexed by natural numbers
definitions.definition: For each natural number m, Eucl(m)=R^m with distance between x and y equal to (sum_{j=1}^m (x_j-y_j)^2)^(1/2). Eucl(0) is the singleton empty tuple. Identify Eucl(m) x R with Eucl(m+1) by concatenating coordinates; its distance is sqrt(dist(x,y)^2+|t-u|^2), throughout, including m=0.

definitions.type: extended nonnegative diameter of a subset of a metric space
definitions.definition: diam(A)=sup{dist(x,y):x,y in A}, with diameter of the empty set zero; it may be infinity. In a native extended metric space the same quantity is ediam(A). At finite diameter it is identified with its nonnegative real value.

definitions.type: unnormalized Hausdorff contents and Hausdorff measures of Euclidean sets
definitions.definition:
For a Euclidean set \(A\), exponent \(s>0\), and scale \(\delta>0\), put

\[
H^s_\delta(A)=\inf\left\{\sum_i(\operatorname{diam}U_i)^s:
 A\subseteq\bigcup_iU_i,\quad\operatorname{diam}U_i\leq\delta\right\},
\qquad H^s(A)=\sup_{\delta>0}H^s_\delta(A).
\]

Covers are countable, with empty members contributing zero.

definitions.type: native Hausdorff measure notation for real exponents on extended metric spaces
definitions.definition: muH[a] denotes Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure a, constructed as the metric measure from the set cost ediam(U)^a, using the Borel measurable structure; its construction is native mkMetric (fun r => r^a). This definition asserts no comparison with H. Native infinite sums and integrals take values in [0,infinity].

binders.type: subset of the ambient extended metric space

definitions.type: native Hausdorff dimension of a subset of an extended metric space
definitions.definition: dimH(A) is the native Mathlib Hausdorff dimension: sup over nonnegative real a such that muH[a](A)=infinity of a, as an element of [0,infinity], with supremum of the empty family zero. The measurable structure used here is Borel.

binders.type: subset of an extended metric space

definitions.type: Hausdorff dimension of a Euclidean set
definitions.definition: dim_H(A) is the usual Hausdorff dimension, represented by dimH(A) on its Euclidean metric. Its meaning is the supremum of nonnegative exponents a for which the native Hausdorff measure muH[a](A) is infinite, with supremum of the empty family zero. Values lie in [0,infinity]. Its equivalence with the critical exponent of the supplied unnormalized covering measure is a proof obligation, not an original hypothesis.

definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the real line and nonnegative Lebesgue integration
definitions.definition: lambda is Lebesgue length measure on R, with its Lebesgue measurable structure. Integrals below are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals valued in [0,infinity]; integration over a measurable set uses the restricted measure. For a set J, 1_J(t) is 1 when t belongs to J and 0 otherwise. The notation |J| means lambda(J).

inputs.statement: For every natural m, every subset A of Eucl(m), and every real s>0, the supplied unnormalized H^s(A) equals native muH[s](A). Moreover dim_H(A)>=0, and: s>dim_H(A) implies H^s(A)=0; 0<s<dim_H(A) implies H^s(A)=infinity; H^s(A)=0 implies dim_H(A)<=s; H^s(A)=infinity implies dim_H(A)>=s. The comparisons allow dim_H(A)=infinity.

output.statement: dim_H(I)=1. For every real a>1, H^a(I)=0. For every real 0<s<1 and delta>0, every countable delta-cover of I with member diameters rho_i has sum_i rho_i>=1 and sum_i rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1); in particular H^s(I)=infinity.

argument.text: For any a>1 and each positive integer k, the k closed intervals [j/k,(j+1)/k], 0<=j<k, cover I. Their diameters are 1/k, and their total a-cost is k*(1/k)^a=k^(1-a), tending to zero as k tends to infinity. At any fixed scale the diameter bound holds for all sufficiently large k. Hence the a-content of I is zero at every positive scale and H^a(I)=0 for every a>1.

Fix delta>0 and an arbitrary countable delta-cover T of I. Ignore empty terms by K={i:T_i nonempty}, and set rho_i=diam(T_i)<=delta. For epsilon>0 the bounded nonempty real set T_i has infimum and supremum, with sup T_i-inf T_i=rho_i. Define the open interval J_i=(inf T_i-epsilon*2^(-i-2),sup T_i+epsilon*2^(-i-2)); it contains T_i and has length rho_i+epsilon*2^(-i-1). These intervals cover I. Countable subadditivity of Lebesgue length, lambda(I)=1, and the geometric sum over K bounded by the full sum over N give 1<=sum_i lambda(J_i)<=sum_i rho_i+epsilon. If sum_i rho_i is infinite the claim is immediate; otherwise letting epsilon decrease to zero gives sum_i rho_i>=1. This holds for the arbitrary cover and scale.

produces.statement: For every positive scale delta_b and every countable delta_b-cover T_b of I, the sum of its nonempty-member diameters is at least 1.

argument.text: For arbitrary 0<s<1, retain delta and T, K, rho. For 0<rho_i<=delta the negative exponent s-1 gives rho_i^(s-1)>=delta^(s-1), hence rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*rho_i. When rho_i=0 the same inequality is 0>=0, since s>0. Sum the inequalities and apply F002: sum_i rho_i^s>=delta^(s-1)*sum_i rho_i>=delta^(s-1). The same holds with empty terms contributing zero. Take the infimum over the arbitrary delta-covers to obtain H^s_delta(I)>=delta^(s-1). Since s-1<0 this lower bound tends to infinity as delta decreases to zero; consequently H^s(I)=infinity for every 0<s<1. This also records the coverwise bound required in the output.

produces.statement: For every 0<s_b<1, H^{s_b}(I)=infinity; for every delta_b>0 every countable delta_b-cover of I with diameter sequence rho_b satisfies sum_i rho_b(i)^{s_b}>=delta_b^(s_b-1).

argument.text: Apply N001 with m=1 on the real Euclidean line: identify a real number with its one-coordinate vector in Eucl(1), preserving distance by the Euclidean formula. F001 gives dim_H(I)<=a for every a>1, hence dim_H(I)<=1. F003 gives dim_H(I)>=s for every 0<s<1, hence dim_H(I)>=1 by real order completeness. Together these yield dim_H(I)=1, and F001,F002,F003 retain all of the additional estimates asserted in the output.
